topic: The IMO Windmill Problem: Geometry in Motion
target_audience: High school students interested in competitive mathematics and geometry.

outline.topic: The IMO Windmill Problem: Geometry in Motion
outline.target_audience: High school students interested in competitive mathematics and geometry.

sections.title: Introduction to 'Willa the Windmill'
sections.content: Introduce the setup: A set of 'S' points on a plane. A character, 'Willa the Robot', holds a long straight laser beam (the line L). The line starts at a point P and rotates clockwise. When the line hits another point Q, that point Q becomes the new pivot point (the center of rotation), and the line continues to rotate.
sections.example: Visual: A scattering of 5 dots (seeds) on a screen. Willa stands at one dot, her laser beam rotating like a clock hand. As it hits a second dot, the 'glow' transfers to that dot, and the beam keeps spinning.

sections.title: Prerequisite: Discrete vs. Continuous Motion
sections.content: Explain the concept of a 'Pivot Switch'. Ensure the audience understands that the line's angle changes continuously, but the center of rotation changes at discrete moments (collisions). Explain that no three points are collinear to keep the transitions clean.
sections.example: Graphic: A side-by-side comparison. A standard clock (fixed center) vs. the 'Windmill' (center jumping from a blue dot to a red dot as the line sweeps across).

sections.title: The Magic Invariant: The Balancing Act
sections.content: Introduce the 'k-points' concept. If there are 'n' points total, the line divides the rest of the points into two sets. Crucially, when the line rotates and hits a point, the number of points on either side of the line remains constant (except for the pivot point itself).
sections.example: Visual: Highlight 2 points in blue on the left of the line and 2 points in red on the right. As the line rotates 180 degrees and swaps pivots, show that there are always 2 points on each side, maintaining a '2-2 balance'.

sections.title: The 180-Degree Flip
sections.content: Demonstrate what happens when the line rotates exactly 180 degrees. Since the 'k-points' on the left must now be on the right (because the line has flipped its orientation), every point must have acted as a pivot at least once to allow the sets to 'permute'.
sections.example: Character Example: Willa starts with a 'North' pointing arrow on her head. After the beam rotates 180 degrees, her arrow points 'South'. To achieve this 'flip' while keeping the side-count constant, the line must have passed through every single point.

sections.title: Summary and the Eternal Cycle
sections.content: Conclude that the windmill process is periodic. Because there are a finite number of points and directions, the system will eventually return to its original state, proving that the 'Windmill' will visit every point infinitely often.
sections.example: Animation: Speed up the rotation. Watch as the laser traces a complex web connecting all dots, eventually returning to the starting point and starting the exact same pattern again.

storyboard.title: Introduction to 'Willa the Windmill'
lecture_lines: Meet Willa and her rotating laser beam line.
She starts at an initial point on the plane.
The beam rotates clockwise around this pivot point.
When hitting another point, the pivot immediately switches.
This creates the "Windmill" motion through the points.
animations: Fade in 5 white points (#FFFFFF) at random positions. Label one 'P'.
Draw a yellow line (#FFFF00) passing through point 'P' at a random angle.
Rotate the yellow line clockwise around 'P'.
As the line hits another white point, label it 'Q' and flash it yellow (#FFFF00).
Change 'P' to white and set the green color (#2ECC71) to 'Q' as the new pivot.

storyboard.title: Prerequisite: Discrete vs. Continuous Motion
lecture_lines: The beam's rotation angle changes continuously over time.
But the center of rotation jumps at discrete hits.
No three points are collinear to keep pivots unique.
animations: Show the yellow line rotating continuously around a green pivot (#2ECC71).
Flash the pivot point green (#2ECC71) as it jumps from one point to another.
Draw a red X (#E74C3C) over a dashed line connecting three points to show no three points are collinear.

storyboard.title: The Magic Invariant: The Balancing Act
lecture_lines: The line divides the other points into two sets.
Let's color points on each side differently to see.
As the pivot switches, the side-counts remain perfectly balanced.
This invariant property holds throughout the entire rotation.
The number of points on each side never changes.
animations: Display 5 points. Place a yellow line (#FFFF00) through a green pivot point (#2ECC71).
Color 2 points on the left blue (#3498DB) and 2 points on the right red (#E74C3C).
Rotate the line clockwise. As it hits a red point, the pivot moves to it.
The old green pivot turns blue (#3498DB), and the hit red point turns green (#2ECC71).
Label the counts: 'Left: 2' and 'Right: 2' to show the balance is preserved.

storyboard.title: The 180-Degree Flip
lecture_lines: Watch what happens after a full 180-degree rotation.
The line's orientation has completely flipped its direction.
Points once on the left are now on the right.
For this swap, the line must hit every point.
This proves the windmill visits every point eventually.
animations: Start with a yellow line (#FFFF00) and an arrow pointing 'North' at the green pivot (#2ECC71).
Rotate the line 180 degrees clockwise. The arrow now points 'South'.
Show the blue (#3498DB) and red (#E74C3C) point sets have swapped sides.
Flash each point yellow (#FFFF00) as the line passes through it during the rotation.
Highlight all points in green (#2ECC71) to show every point has been a pivot once.

storyboard.title: Summary and the Eternal Cycle
lecture_lines: Since the state is finite, the process is periodic.
The windmill returns to its start and repeats forever.
This beautiful cycle connects every point in the set.
animations: Fast-forward the rotation, leaving thin gray (#808080) traces of the line's path.
The yellow line (#FFFF00) returns to the initial point P and the initial angle.
Pulse all points in green (#2ECC71) to signify the cycle is complete and will repeat.

issues.description:
[section_1] Implement Manim code for 'Introduction to Willa'. 
Steps: 
1. Fade in 5 white points at random positions. Label one 'P'.
2. Draw a yellow line through 'P' at a random angle.
3. Rotate the line clockwise around 'P'.
4. On hitting another point 'Q', flash it yellow.
5. Switch pivot to 'Q' (change color to green) and continue rotation.
Lecture lines: Meet Willa and her laser beam; she starts at a point; rotates clockwise; pivot switches on hit; creates the 'Windmill' motion.

[section_2] Implement Manim code for 'Discrete vs. Continuous Motion'.
Steps:
1. Show continuous rotation of a yellow line around a green pivot.
2. Flash the pivot green as it jumps between points.
3. Use a red X over a dashed line connecting three points to demonstrate the 'no three points are collinear' rule.
Lecture lines: Angle changes continuously; center jumps at discrete hits; no three points are collinear for uniqueness.

[section_3] Implement Manim code for 'The Magic Invariant'.
Steps:
1. Show 5 points with a yellow line through a green pivot.
2. Color points on sides: 2 blue (left), 2 red (right).
3. Rotate clockwise; when hitting a red point, pivot moves.
4. Old pivot becomes blue, new pivot becomes green.
5. Display 'Left: 2' and 'Right: 2' labels to show invariant balance.
Lecture lines: Line divides points into two sets; color points to see; side-counts remain balanced during pivot switches; this invariant holds throughout.

[section_4] Implement Manim code for 'The 180-Degree Flip'.
Steps:
1. Start with yellow line and North-pointing arrow at green pivot.
2. Rotate 180 degrees clockwise; arrow flips to South.
3. Show blue and red sets have swapped sides.
4. Flash each point yellow as the line hits it.
5. Highlight all points green at the end.
Lecture lines: 180-degree rotation flips orientation; sides swap; line must hit every point to achieve this; proves windmill visits every point.

[section_5] Implement Manim code for 'Summary and the Eternal Cycle'.
Steps:
1. Fast-forward rotation with thin gray traces of the line's path.
2. Return to starting point P and original angle.
3. Pulse all points in green to show cycle completion.
Lecture lines: Process is periodic due to finite states; returns to start and repeats; connects every point in a cycle.
